technical.summary: Long-term trend structure is bullish but price action remains weak with multiple short-term bearish signals and price below key moving averages; insufficient confluence for high-probability entry.

fundamental.summary: ABBV shows no actionable smart money signals with zero insider activity, no institutional positioning data, absent government contracts, no lobbying activity, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 85 days present material risk.

sentiment.summary: No actionable congressional signal; mixed retail sentiment (bearish 38.5% vs bullish 24.1%) with neutral fear-greed reading (58/100) and absent news data provide insufficient conviction for directional bias.

risk.summary: Extreme VIX crisis (160.4), inverted yield curve, FOMC event today, and negative macro score (-7) create severe near-term headwinds; earnings in 85 days adds secondary risk layer.

debate.key_bull_argument: Long-term trend structure (EMA 50/200 and SMA 50/200 bullish, supertrend bullish) provides directional bias and price near support (134.89) offers defined risk entry for swing traders.
debate.key_bear_argument: Extreme macro headwinds (VIX crisis at 160.4, inverted yield curve, FOMC event today), price below all key moving averages, weak technical confluence (RSI 36, stoch bearish cross, Ichimoku below cloud), zero fundamental conviction, and high earnings risk in 85 days create unacceptable risk/reward for entry.

decision.entry_rationale: Already holding ABBV with 21 existing Health Care positions creates dangerous sector concentration; macro environment (VIX 160.4, inverted yield curve, FOMC today) presents unacceptable near-term risk despite bullish long-term structure.
decision.primary_risk: Extreme VIX crisis and FOMC event today combined with price below all key moving averages creates high probability of immediate drawdown before long-term trend can develop.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on unfavourable risk/reward
decision.portfolio_note: Existing ABBV position plus 21 Health Care holdings (37% of portfolio) already create excessive sector concentration; adding to this position violates prudent diversification and increases portfolio fragility in crisis macro environment.
